title: fix(cli): reset slash-command conflict dedupe when conflicts reappear

triage_metadata.reasoning: The issue clearly describes a logic bug in SlashCommandConflictHandler where notifiedConflicts grows indefinitely and prevents re-notifying users if a previously resolved slash command conflict reappears. It specifies the affected file, root cause, expected behavior, and a suggested fix.
triage_metadata.effort_reasoning: The fix is localized to a single source file (packages/cli/src/services/SlashCommandConflictHandler.ts) where handleConflicts needs to sync notifiedConflicts with active conflict keys from incoming payloads. Unit testing in packages/cli/src/services/SlashCommandConflictHandler.test.ts is straightforward.

summary.problem: SlashCommandConflictHandler retains notified conflict keys permanently in a process-lifetime set, preventing re-notification if a conflict is resolved and subsequently reappears.
summary.root_cause: handleConflicts adds conflict keys to notifiedConflicts without ever pruning or resetting keys when conflicts are no longer present in subsequent event payloads.
summary.context: SlashCommandConflictHandler batches conflict events to display user feedback when command name collisions occur. Deduplication should track currently active conflicts rather than all historical conflicts forever.

steps: In SlashCommandConflictHandler.ts, update handleConflicts to construct a Set of active conflict keys from payload.conflicts.
Remove keys from this.notifiedConflicts that are not present in the current active conflict keys set.
Filter payload.conflicts against this.notifiedConflicts to identify new conflicts, and add new keys to this.notifiedConflicts.
Schedule a flush if there are any new conflicts to notify.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: When a previously resolved conflict reappears in a subsequent payload, SlashCommandConflictHandler notifies the user again.
verification_steps: In SlashCommandConflictHandler.test.ts, add a unit test that simulates a conflict event and verifies feedback is emitted.
Simulate an event payload where the conflict is resolved (not present).
Simulate the conflict event again and verify that feedback is emitted once more.
